To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

candidate dietary phytochemical agents, green tea extracts, broccoli sprout extracts, epigallocatechin, sulforaphane, phenethyl isothiocyante, and benzyl isithiocyanate induce the phase II enzyme NQO1 at mRNA and protein level in normal human bronchical epithelial cells and immortalized human bronchiol epithelial cells, but not in lung adenocarcinaoma cell line.
NQO-1 protein expression was significantly induced by sulforaphane, but not by the green tea extract or the broccoli sprout extract, in primary normal human bronchical epithelial cells.
NQO-1 is more responsive than GSTP1 to the chemopreventative agents tested and there is a discordance between single agents and complex mixture effects.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of candidate dietary phytochemical agents in human lung cells, which are the target cells of lung cancer.
identifying and characterizing novel chemopreventives for the prevention and treatment of cancer.
the effects of candidate dietary phytochemical agents on phase II enzymes in human lung cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
GTE, BTE and SFN are inducers of NQO1 and GSTP1 in NHBE cells and that NQO-1 is a more sensitive marker than GSTP1.
dietary phytochemical exposure modulates phase II enzymes in a cell- and phytochemical-specific manner.
the studied phytochemicals are able to modulate expression of NQO1 and GSTP1 in normal human lung cells, but not in lung cancer cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the phytochemicals we studied, especially SFN, have a potential to modulate the lung cell phase II enzyme expression, which may be a mechanism for their cancer prevention activity.
NQO-1 may be a more sensitive marker for the chemoprevention effect of phytochemicals than GST-P1.
the effects on phase II enzymes GST P1 and NQ0 1 in human lung cell lines by phytochemicals are cell- and agent-dependent.
The main takeaway from our work is that

dietary phytochemical mixtures may have a greater effect on inducing lung cell phase II enzymes than their individual constituents, suggesting that the effects of complex mixtures cannot be predicted based on the effects of their constituents.
dietary chemopreventives may be more effective when consumed as a whole mixture rather than individual components.
the effects of phytochemicals are not additive, but synergistic.
